To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fibrin constructs mixed with TGF-beta3 loaded in nanoparticles can be used to promote chondrogenesis and hyaline cartilaginous tissue formation by BMSCs in vitro and in subcutaneous sites.

the effects of TGF-beta loaded in nanoparticles mixed with fibrin constructs on BMSC chondrogenesis were investigated by evaluating specific cartilage extracelluar matrix components in vitro as well as in vivo using rabbit BMSCs as a special cell source.
BMSCs embedded into fibrin hydrogel mixed with growth factors loaded into nanoparticles can be used for cartilage regeneration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technology for cartilage repair.

the development of an injectable fibrin matrix that is loaded with TGF-3 in nanoparticle form for the in vitro and in vitro chondrogenesis and transplantation of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells.
developing a novel system for cartilage repair that uses a fibrin hydrogel as a three-dimensional scaffold and a growth factor delivery system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of fibrin construct that contained BMSC and were provided with a sustained level of growth factors for long period of time enable formation of hyalne cartilage tissue in both in vitro and vivo.
the use of fibrin scaffolds that contained BMSC and were provided with a sustained level of growth factor for a long period enabled formation of hyal cartilage tissue in vivo and in vitro.
the use of fibrin scaffolds containing TGF-beta3 nanoparticles is a promising approach for cartilage tissue engineering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to demonstrate that the combination of fibrin and growth factor-loaded nanoparticle is effective in inducing chondrogenesis in vitro and in a nude mouse model.

we have shown that BMSCs are a suitable cell source for cartilage tissue engineering, and we have demonstrated the effectiveness of the use of fibrin matrix mixed together with growth factor-loaded nanoparticles for cartilage tissue regeneration.

we have demonstrated that fibrin hydrogel constructs that were provided with growth factor-loaded nanoparticles could induce the differentiation of rabbit bone marrow stromal cells to chondrocytes in vitro and in a nude mouse model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fibrin constructs containing BMSCs and growth factors may be used as a scaffold for cartilage tissue engineering.
the use of fibrin matrix with growth factor-loaded nanoparticles can be used to enhance chondrogenesis in vitro and in an animal model.
the fibrin constructs that contain TGF-beta loaded nanoparticles can be useful for the treatment of cartilage defects.
